# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection
**Capture:** 2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap | **LAN:** 10.11.26.0/24 | **DC:** 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODE-DC)

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | consistent across all evidence |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | ARP src for 10.11.26.183 |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (workgroup/NetBIOS name NEMOTODES) | NBNS |
| Domain | nemotoads.health (AD domain via LDAP/SRV queries) | DNS |
| Logged-in user | oboomwald | Kerberos `CNameString`, requests between 10.11.26.183 and DC 10.11.26.3 |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access tool). **Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET fired `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, and `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response` against this exact flow. This is independently corroborated by protocol content pulled directly from the pcap: TCP stream 77 (10.11.26.183:53362 ↔ 194.180.191.64:443) is plaintext HTTP (not TLS, despite the 443 destination port) carrying `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` requests with bodies `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1`, answered by `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)` with encrypted `CMD=ENCD / DATA=...` payloads — the exact NetSupport client-gateway polling protocol. A `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (returning victim geo-coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877`) further confirms genuine NetSupport client code is running on the host.

## Delivery Chain

1. **Lure/redirect:** DNS resolution of `classicgrand.com` (→ 213.246.109.5) at 08:50:11 UTC, immediately followed by resolution of `modandcrackedapk.com` (→ 193.42.38.139) at 08:50:14 UTC — a known "cracked-software" lure domain that Suricata flagged as a **ZPHP domain** (`ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup / TLS SNI`), consistent with a fake-CAPTCHA/fake-download page pattern used to trick users into fetching a malicious installer.
2. **Payload retrieval:** A large encrypted TLS session to 193.42.38.139:443 (SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`) transferred ~10 MB inbound to the victim, sized consistent with a bundled installer/RAT payload. Content is TLS-encrypted and could not be extracted.
3. **C2 establishment:** Within seconds, NetSupport RAT began beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443, first beacon 08:50:45 UTC, continuing at roughly 60-second intervals through 09:43:29 UTC (last packet in capture) — an active, persistent RAT session for the duration of the capture.

**Note (out of scope, benign context, not attributed to this actor):** SMB/MS-EFSR and legacy SMBv1 alerts between 10.11.26.183 and DC 10.11.26.3 (`EfsRpcOpenFileRaw`, `SMB IPC$` access, `ntlmssp` overflow signature) reflect normal/legacy AD domain-join SMB chatter on this exercise network, not observed lateral-movement tooling from the RAT; no malicious SMB payload or scanning pattern was found in that traffic.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | HTTP `CMD=POLL/ENCD` beacon traffic, TCP stream 77; ETPRO NetSupport RAT CnC alerts |
| Domain (delivery/lure) | **modandcrackedapk.com** (→ 193.42.38.139) | DNS query + TLS SNI; ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP alerts |
| Domain (delivery/redirect) | **classicgrand.com** (→ 213.246.109.5) | DNS query at 08:50:11 UTC preceding lure domain; TLS SNI on stream to 213.246.109.5 |
| URL (C2 checkin) | **http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm** | HTTP POST requests, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, repeated ~every 60s from 08:50:45 to 09:43:29 UTC |
| URL (NetSupport geo-check, supporting tool artifact) | **http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp** | HTTP GET, response body `33.7488,-84.3877` |
| C2 protocol string | `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)` | Reassembled TCP stream 77 |

No downloadable executable, DLL, or file object with a hash could be extracted from the pcap — the payload delivery over 193.42.38.139:443 and 213.246.109.5:443 was TLS-encrypted, so no file name or SHA256 can be grounded from this capture alone.

## Benign Context (not indicators)
`api.msn.com`, `login.live.com`, `*.office.net`, `*.microsoft.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `bing.com`, `gstatic.com`, `google*.com`, `createsend1.com`, `jquery` CDN — standard Windows/Office/browser telemetry and update traffic, unrelated to the intrusion.

## Summary
User **oboomwald** on Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b) visited a cracked-software lure chain (`classicgrand.com` → `modandcrackedapk.com`) around 08:50 UTC on 2024-11-26 and downloaded a payload that installed **NetSupport RAT**. The RAT immediately began polling its C2 at **194.180.191.64:443** using the NetSupport client-gateway protocol (`POLL`/`ENCD` over plaintext HTTP on port 443, `NetSupport Manager/1.3` user-agent) and remained active, beaconing roughly every 60 seconds, through the end of the capture at 09:43 UTC.
